title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's Wedding Had an NDA 'With Teeth,' Guests Reveal
excerpt: Two weeks after the Madison Square Garden ceremony, details are slowly emerging about the 1,000-guest event — including Avril Lavigne performing 'Sk8er Boi,' Paul McCartney's rare Beatles song, and a very effective non-disclosure agreement.
body:
• Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce married at Madison Square Garden on July 3 with roughly 1,000 guests, including Selena Gomez, Bradley Cooper, and Gigi Hadid.
  • Guests signed an NDA described as having "teeth," with invitations sent via anonymous texts that some guests mistook for phishing scams.
  • Performers included Paul McCartney (who played a Beatles song he hadn't performed since the 1960s), Stevie Nicks, and Avril Lavigne singing "Sk8er Boi."
  • The couple donated $26 million to charity during their wedding weekend, and the venue was transformed into an intimate garden setting in peach, white, and green.

Two weeks after Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce said their vows at Madison Square Garden, the world's most anticipated wedding remains remarkably under wraps. No photos have leaked. The dress remains a mystery. But the guests, slowly and carefully, have begun to talk.

And what they describe is an event that was equal parts spectacle and intimacy — a wedding where Paul McCartney played a Beatles song he hadn't performed since the 1960s, where Avril Lavigne rocked "Sk8er Boi," where Adam Sandler officiated, and where a non-disclosure agreement kept it all sealed tight.

https://x.com/OKMagazine/status/2078658323902070820

The NDA Had Teeth

Country star Brad Paisley, who attended with his wife Kimberly Williams-Paisley, described a carefully controlled invitation process in an interview with The Associated Press. "They were very clear with the invite," Paisley said. "If you're getting this, you mean a lot to us."

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk confirmed he had signed an NDA before attending. Despite that, he told People magazine at the TIME100 Sports Gala that it was "genuinely so much fun. The whole aura, the whole room was just full of excitement and fun and love."

Pat McAfee, the ESPN sports analyst, nearly missed the entire event. He described on his show how the invitation came via text from an unknown number with a link — which he promptly deleted, thinking it was a phishing scam. He deleted the follow-up too. It took a personal text from Kelce to convince him it was real.

"Travis had to text me and say, 'Hey, this is a real text.' I'm like, 'What an honor.' I did not think that would happen."

— Pat McAfee, ESPN host

MSG Transformed

AMC CEO Adam Aron, in a since-deleted post on X, described Madison Square Garden as virtually unrecognizable — transformed into an intimate garden setting draped in peach, white, and green, with childhood photos of the bride and groom displayed throughout.

Kristin Juszczyk, who attended with her husband Kyle, told People: "No, it was absolutely gorgeous. I think it was exactly what her vision was and it came to life." She added: "I wanna journal that night so I never forget."

Two anonymous attendees who spoke to NBC News described a photo-lined entry tunnel, heartwarming vows, and reception sets from McCartney, Stevie Nicks, and Swift herself. "You would think the bride would be the one crying more," they said, "but it was actually Travis that was more emotional."

The Entertainment

The performer lineup has emerged as one of the wedding's most talked-about details. McAfee revealed on his show that McCartney played a song "he hasn't played since 1960-something for the first time ever" — reportedly "I Want to Hold Your Hand." Stevie Nicks also performed, with Swift joining both artists on stage.

Avril Lavigne's appearance was perhaps the biggest surprise. The pop-punk icon performed her 2002 anthem "Sk8er Boi," joining McCartney and Nicks in what McAfee described as an informal jam session: "One would just call out the other and then they would come up and then they would just do their shit."

The Guest List

Among the roughly 1,000 guests were Dakota Johnson, Patrick Mahomes, Lena Dunham, Gigi Hadid, Jack Antonoff, Bradley Cooper, Mariska Hargitay, and Selena Gomez. The appearance of Karlie Kloss, once one of Swift's closest friends before a rumored falling out, raised eyebrows.

Shaquille O'Neal, who did not receive an invite, offered his congratulations at the Fanatics Fest in New York: "May it last forever."

The couple also made headlines for donating $26 million to charity during their wedding weekend, according to Aron's deleted post. Swift and Kelce, both 36, had announced their engagement in an August 2025 Instagram post after dating since 2023.
